I5.quote: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) arrays were dispersed in Na2CO3 solution and co-precipitated with metal nitrite to form long CNTs (over 500 mm) intercrossed Cu/Zn/Al/Zr catalyst (CD703).

notes: Catalysis paper (CNT-promoted Cu/Zn/Al/Zr methanol/DME synthesis catalyst). Hydrogen appears only as a reactant in CO/CO2 hydrogenation (H2/CO = 2.0, H2/CO2 = 3.0, 4.0-5.0 MPa; main, p. 3, Section 2) and as a 5% H2/95% N2 catalyst reduction gas; no H2 uptake by a sorbent is measured. Hydrogen storage on CNTs is mentioned only as a cited literature finding: 'CNTs can reversibly adsorb and store a considerably greater amount of hydrogen [12]' (main, p. 4, Section 3.5). Not theoretical_only (experimental work), not electrochemical, primary article, is_retracted false in record.json and no retraction notice in the PDF text, so the I1 failure falls to no_conditions_stated.
